text:
nina: hey all — accepted the org invite but can't see private repos. web shows 'SAML SSO: authorization required' and gh CLI shows 'SSO: NOT authorized'. clone over SSH -> Permission denied (publickey).
alex: did you accept with your work account? sometimes people accept with personal accounts if you're signed in elsewhere.
nina: positive it's nina@redwood.ai. But I did have Authenticator 2FA on my phone from a side project, could that matter?
people-ops: 2FA itself is fine. The common flow is: 1) verify your work email in GitHub profile, 2) accept the org invite while signed in as that account, 3) click "Authorize SSO" on https://github.com/orgs/redwood which redirects to Okta.
infra-oncall: also check Settings -> SSH and GPG keys to ensure your SSH key is attached to the same account. If you have keys on a personal account, SSH will fail even after SSO authorized.
nina: tried to authorize SSO but I don't see the button on the org page in my normal browser.
alex: browser extensions or cached sessions can hide it. Try incognito or a different browser. Also confirm you're not logged into personal GitHub in another tab.
nina: incognito showed the button. clicked it, got sent to Okta, approved. gh now shows SSO: authorized.
git-bot: tip: after SSO authorize, run `gh auth refresh` and restart any GUI clients (GitHub Desktop/VSCode) so tokens refresh.
nina: did that and now I can view repos. SSH still failed until I re-added my SSH key to the correct account and ran `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. then `ssh -T git@github.com` says welcome.
people-ops: thanks for the troubleshooting notes — we'll add a short onboarding item: verify work email primary, try incognito if authorize button missing, watch out for SSH keys tied to other accounts, and call out Authenticator/2FA only if it blocks login. welcome! :tada:
